title: Theoretical and computational bounds for m-cycles of the 3n+1-problem
relevant_concepts: continued fraction convergents of log 2 / log 3
status: read in full, 21 September 2026, from the PDF Philippe placed on the Desktop (Acta Arithmetica's archive refuses this environment); local copy literature/sources/simons-de-weger-2005-collatz-m-cycles.pdf, untracked
notes: Acta Arithmetica 117.1 (2005) 51-70, received 4.12.2003, revised 10.11.2004. CORRECTION OF THE EARLIER RECORD: the floor is X_0 = 301 * 2^50 > 3.3889 * 10^17 (Roosendaal, 10 November 2004), not 2.5 * 2^60; the 'later 75' belongs to Simons 2008 at the larger floor. NOTATION: K odd numbers, L even numbers in the cycle, m local minima x_i = 2^(k_i) a_i - 1, local maxima y_i; Lambda = (K+L) log 2 - K log 3; delta = log 3/log 2 = [1;1,1,2,2,3,1,5,2,23,2,2,1,1,55,...]. THE TEMPLATE. Section 2: the chain equation 3^(k_i) a_i - 1 = 2^(k_(i+1)+l_i) a_(i+1) - 2^(l_i), the matrix M with det = (-1)^(m-1) Delta, Delta = 2^(K+L) - 3^K > 0, m-cycles in bijection with positive integer solutions (Boehm-Sontacchi). Lemma 4: 0 < Lambda < sum_i 1/x_i over the local minima (from the chain equation and log(1+x) < x); Corollary 5: Lambda < m/x_min <= m/X_0. Lemma 6 (chaining): x_(i+1) < b^delta x_i^delta with b = (1 + 1/X_0)/2^(1/delta) = 0.64576. Lemma 7: Lambda < m c_m 2^(-(delta-1)/(delta^m-1) K) with c_m -> 0.30576, from the product of the local minima against 2^K (each x_i + 1 >= 2^(k_i)). Lemma 8: delta K < K + L < 1.000001 delta K. Lemma 9: Legendre and best-approximation facts. Lemma 10 (generalized Crandall): if q_n + q_(n+1) <= (log 2) X_0/m then K > q_n; Corollary 11 tabulates it (2 <= m <= 19: K > q_31 > 5.7509e15; 38 <= m <= 256: K > 4.3116e14; ...; m >= 131993765: K > 1.7095 m). Lemma 12 (Rhin): Lambda > exp(-13.3 (0.46057 + log K)), which is Rhin's Proposition |Lambda| >= H^(-13.3) at H = K + L with Lemma 8, 0.46057 being log delta -- so the laboratory's transcription of Rhin since Paper A is this Lemma 12, in the odd count. Corollary 13: x_min < m e^(13.3(0.46057+log K)). Lemma 14: K < K_1(m), the largest solution of Rhin's bound against Lemma 7 (k_1(m) = K_1/(m delta^m) -> 15.107); Lemma 15: no m-cycles for 2 <= m <= 57 (K_1(57) < 2.8037e14 against Corollary 11's 4.3116e14). Section 6.2: the reduced bound K_2(m) through the champion partial quotients A(m) of delta (continued fraction to a_200001); Lemma 16: K < K_2(m) for 58 <= m <= 515619; Lemma 17: no m-cycles for 2 <= m <= 63 (K_2(63) < 4.0367e14). Section 7: de Weger's approximation lattice with C = round(X_0 log 2 K_2(m)/(2m)), reduced basis, brute force over points of norm <= K_2(m); Lemma 18: (a) none for 64 <= m <= 68; (b) 69 <= m <= 72 the possible (K, L) are listed with the floor that kills each (577..706 * 2^50, expected 2004-2008); (c) 73 <= m <= 90 solution counts 8 to 23181, K >= 5.2673e15. THEOREM 3: (a) Brox finiteness; (b) no nontrivial m-cycles for 1 <= m <= 68 (m = 1 Steiner 1977); (c), (d) explicit bounds K < 1.3993 m delta^m etc. for m >= 73. Conclusion: 'with the present techniques one cannot go much further... an entirely new idea seems to be needed'; the border 68/69 is set by X_0. WHAT THE LABORATORY DID WITH IT (docs/problems/juggler_negative_m_cycles.md): the template transposed to the 3n-1 map, Lemmas 4, 6, 7, 10 rederived on the negative side with constant one in Lemma 4 and u' < u^delta/2 exactly in Lemma 6, the admissible lengths enumerated exactly by the three-gap walk in place of Corollary 11 and K_2, Rhin used at H = the cycle length; no lattice step. THEIR LADDER at 301 * 2^50: tables 57, continued-fraction reduction 63, lattice 68; the transposition's number at the same floor is recorded in that dossier for comparison. The Baker half does not transfer to the Juggler (see the earlier note); it transfers to 3n-1.
